effects: The function only emits Message(msg.sender, text, text). No ETH or token moves, no approval is set and no on-chain state changes for the signer.

Outside the chain, the text (JSON such as {"action":"withdraw","pubkeys":[...]}) asks P2P's backend to exit the listed validators. The contract does not check the action, the keys or whether the signer controls them.
formats.shown: The intent 'Withdrawal message' and one field, 'Public keys', that shows the whole message text raw, JSON included.

findings.title: send: the intent and label assume a withdraw action, but the text is free-form and unchecked.
findings.evidence: P2pMessageSender.sol send(): `emit Message(msg.sender, text, text);` does not check the content. descriptor: intent "Withdrawal message" is fixed, and field label "Public keys" sits on `#.text`. That field also carries the "action" key (case 0: {"action":"withdraw","pubkeys":[...]}). A message with another action or no keys would still read 'Withdrawal message' / 'Public keys'.
findings.fix: Use a neutral intent such as 'Send message to P2P Staking (e.g. validator withdrawal request)' and label the field 'Message'.

findings.title: send: the off-chain result (validator exit by P2P) is not enforced on-chain or shown in the descriptor.
findings.evidence: P2pMessageSender.sol send() only emits an event. Any exit of the listed validators is done by P2P's backend reading the log. Case 0 mined: effects [] and signerNet []. Reader 'unsure': where the withdrawn funds go and whether the request can be undone.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. A short note in the intent or label that this only signals a request could help.

cases.notes: The mined tx has no token or ETH movement and no approvals. The reader correctly saw nothing leaving or arriving and read the message as a withdrawal request for 4 validator keys. That matches the JSON. The raw JSON is long but readable.
